/api/dashboards:
    get:
      description: Returns a paginated list of dashboards. Each result includes title, description, tags, and metadata, but not the full panel layout. Use `GET /api/dashboards/{id}` to retrieve the complete state.
      operationId: get-dashboards
      parameters:
        - description: The page of results to return.
          in: query
          name: page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 1
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: The number of results to return per page.
          in: query
          name: per_page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 20
            maximum: 1000
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: Filters results by `title` and `description` using Elasticsearch [`simple_query_string`](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/query-dsl-simple-query-string-query) syntax. Multi-word terms require all words to match.
          in: query
          name: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
        - description: A tag ID to include. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are included.
          in: query
          name: tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag ID to exclude. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag name to include. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are included. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are included.
          in: query
          name: tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array

- **Traffic:** `response` (the HTTP status code), `bytes`, `url`, `request`, `extension`, `referer`
- **Visitors:** `clientip`, `agent`, `machine.os`, `geo.src`/`geo.dest`, `geo.coordinates`
- **Other:** `host`, `tags`, `memory`, `machine.ram`

I looked at the field list only; I didn't run any queries against the documents themselves.

**2. Dashboard "EFF-fd7b94ca Web logs overview"** (id `01157bc5-ab2e-47a1-8f59-bb2926a3f5b4`, default time range the last 7 days) has eight panels:
- Four single-number tiles:
  - Total requests
  - Unique visitors (distinct `clientip`)
  - Average response size in bytes
  - Count of 5xx errors
- A stacked bar chart of requests over time, split by response code
- A donut chart of requests by response code
- A table of the top 10 URLs, with request count and total bytes
- A donut chart of requests by visitor operating system

**3. Rule "EFF-fd7b94ca 5xx spike"** (id `7b8aeb83-51c8-4d1a-873b-20a9bcbb4f2a`) is an Elasticsearch query rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`:
- It runs every minute.
- It counts requests whose response code starts with "5" over the last 5 minutes and fires when the count is above 10.
- Kibana switched on a setting by default that skips requests already counted in the previous run. With a 1-minute check over a 5-minute window, that would have undercounted, so I turned it off. Each check now counts every 5xx request in the full 5 minutes.
- It has no actions attached, so when it fires the alert only shows up in Kibana. If you want an email or Slack message, it needs a connector added.

- **Visitors:** `clientip`, `agent`, `machine.os`, `geo.src`/`geo.dest`, `geo.coordinates`
- **Other:** `host`, `tags`, `memory`, `machine.ram`

I looked at the field list only; I didn't run any queries against the documents themselves.

**2. Dashboard "EFF-fd7b94ca Web logs overview"** (id `01157bc5-ab2e-47a1-8f59-bb2926a3f5b4`, default time range the last 7 days) has eight panels:
- Four single-number tiles:
  - Total requests
  - Unique visitors (distinct `clientip`)
  - Average response size in bytes
  - Count of 5xx errors
- A stacked bar chart of requests over time, split by response code
- A donut chart of requests by response code
- A table of the top 10 URLs, with request count and total bytes
- A donut chart of requests by visitor operating system

**3. Rule "EFF-fd7b94ca 5xx spike"** (id `7b8aeb83-51c8-4d1a-873b-20a9bcbb4f2a`) is an Elasticsearch query rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`:
- It runs every minute.
- It counts requests whose response code starts with "5" over the last 5 minutes and fires when the count is above 10.
- Kibana switched on a setting by default that skips requests already counted in the previous run. With a 1-minute check over a 5-minute window, that would have undercounted, so I turned it off. Each check now counts every 5xx request in the full 5 minutes.
- It has no actions attached, so when it fires the alert only shows up in Kibana. If you want an email or Slack message, it needs a connector added.
